newsitem.title: UK: UK's Major says needs persuading to join EMU.
newsitem.headline: UK's Major says needs persuading to join EMU.

text.p: Prime Minister John Major said on Monday he would need "a lot of persuading" before he would take Britain into a single European currency.
Speaking in Leeds, Northern England, to senior pupils at a secondary school, Major also said it would be "an economic catastrophe" if the single currency were set up and then collapsed.

Major recalled that he had been the Chancellor of the Exchequer who had taken Britain into the EU's Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM) in 1990 but said that a few years later the mechanism had collapsed, causing "great damage" to Europe.
"If that were to happen to a single currency the damage would be magnified several times over. It would be a much bigger economic catastrophe," Major said.

Going on to the question of whether he could ever take Britain into a single currency, he said: "I would need a lot of persuading but if I were persuaded, I would come back and I would try to persuade the cabinet."
Major said he was very hopeful that a new Conservative government would be able to cut taxes but could not definitively promise this.
"At the moment it looks as if the economy is set fair for fairly stable growth over the next two or three years, of 2-1/2 to 2-3/4 percent," Major said.
He said that provided this was achieved and the growth in public expenditure was restrained, this would open up a wedge to allow tax cuts.
"We propose to keep the growth in public expenditure below the growth of the economy. I think we will be able to do it. We will wait and see whether we can" he said.
